subject: physics
title: Energy transfers
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Energy transfers — AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification, section 4.2.4.
meta_desc: GCSE Physics (AQA) practice covering Energy transfers, specification section 4.2.4.
final_note: You worked through Energy transfers — 31 specification statements.

concepts.term: Power transfer in a circuit device
concepts.def: The power of a circuit device is the energy it transfers each second. A device with a larger power transfers more energy in the same time. Power is measured in watts, W, and 1 W is a transfer of 1 J each second.

concepts.term: power = potential difference × current (P = V I)
concepts.def: The power transfer in any circuit device equals the potential difference across it multiplied by the current through it: P = V I, with P in watts, W, V in volts, V, and I in amperes, A. This equation must be recalled and applied.

The power transfer in a device can also be found from the current through it and its resistance: P = I² R, with P in watts, W, I in amperes, A, and R in ohms, Ω. Because the current is squared, doubling the current gives four times the power.
The quantity symbol for potential difference is V and it is measured in volts, whose unit symbol is also V. It is the quantity that appears in P = V I and in E = Q V.
The quantity symbol for current is I and it is measured in amperes, A. The word amp is acceptable in place of ampere.
The quantity symbol for resistance is R and it is measured in ohms, whose unit symbol is Ω. Resistance appears in the power equation P = I² R.
The watt is the unit of power, with unit symbol W. Because power is energy transferred per second, a power of 1 W means 1 joule is transferred every second.

concepts.term: Appliances are designed to bring about energy transfers
concepts.def: Everyday electrical appliances are built so that the electrical work done on them produces a particular useful energy transfer, for example turning a motor or heating water. The design of the appliance decides which transfer happens.

concepts.term: What the energy transferred depends on
concepts.def: The amount of energy an appliance transfers depends on two things: how long the appliance is switched on for, and the power of the appliance. Neither one alone decides the total energy transferred.
In appliances such as a food mixer, an electric drill or a washing machine drum, energy is transferred electrically from the battery or the ac mains to the kinetic energy store of the rotating motor.

In appliances such as a kettle, a toaster or an electric heater, energy is transferred electrically from the battery or the ac mains to the thermal energy store of the heating element and of whatever it heats.

concepts.term: Batteries and ac mains as supplies
concepts.def: Domestic appliances are supplied either by batteries, which provide a direct current, or by the ac mains, which provides an alternating current. Either supply can do electrical work on the appliance and bring about the same kind of energy transfer.
Work is done when charge flows in a circuit. The power supply does work pushing charge through the components, and that work is the energy transferred electrically to the components.

concepts.term: energy transferred = power × time (E = P t)
concepts.def: The energy transferred by electrical work equals the power of the device multiplied by the time it operates: E = P t, with E in joules, J, P in watts, W, and t in seconds, s. The time must be converted to seconds before use.

concepts.term: energy transferred = charge flow × potential difference (E = Q V)
concepts.def: The energy transferred by electrical work also equals the charge that flows multiplied by the potential difference it moves through: E = Q V, with E in joules, J, Q in coulombs, C, and V in volts, V.
The joule is the unit of energy transferred, with unit symbol J. Both E = P t and E = Q V give the energy transferred in joules when the other quantities are in their own standard units.
The quantity symbol for time is t and it is measured in seconds, s. A time given in minutes or hours must be converted to seconds before it is substituted into E = P t.
The quantity symbol for charge flow is Q and it is measured in coulombs, C. Charge flow is the amount of charge that passes a point, not the rate at which it passes, which is the current.

concepts.term: Power rating of a domestic appliance
concepts.def: The power rating printed on an appliance states the power in watts it transfers when in normal use. A higher power rating means a faster change in stored energy: a 2000 W kettle empties the mains supply of energy and fills the water's thermal store far faster than a 60 W lamp fills its surroundings.
The National Grid is a system of cables and transformers linking power stations to consumers. It is the network through which electrical power reaches homes, schools and factories.
A step-up transformer is used to increase the potential difference from the power station to the transmission cables, so that the same power can be transferred with a much smaller current.
A step-down transformer is used to decrease the potential difference, to a much lower value, for domestic use. It sits between the transmission cables and the consumer.

concepts.term: Why the National Grid is efficient
concepts.def: For a given power, P = V I means that raising the potential difference lowers the current in the transmission cables. The power wasted heating the cables is given by P = I² R, so a smaller current wastes far less energy. Transformers therefore make the grid an efficient way to transfer energy over long distances.
Electrical power is transferred from power stations to consumers using the National Grid. The grid transfers the power that power stations generate; it does not generate or store it.

concepts.term: Linking power, potential difference, current and energy over time
concepts.def: The power of a circuit device is set by the potential difference across it and the current through it (P = V I), and it is also the energy transferred over a given time (E = P t, so P = E ÷ t). The two routes must give the same power for the same device.

mcqs.q: A lamp has a potential difference of 12 V across it and a current of 2.5 A through it. What is the power transfer in the lamp?
mcqs.explain: P = V I = 12 × 2.5 = 30 W, with pd in volts and current in amperes giving power in watts.

mcqs.q: A current of 3.0 A passes through a resistor of resistance 5.0 Ω. What is the power transfer in the resistor?
Which row gives the correct unit for every quantity in the equation P = I² R?
options: power in watts, current in amperes, resistance in ohms
power in joules, current in amperes, resistance in ohms
power in watts, current in coulombs, resistance in ohms
power in watts, current in amperes, resistance in volts
mcqs.explain: These are the units the specification states for P, I and R.

mcqs.q: The potential difference across a fixed resistor is doubled. What happens to the power transfer in the resistor?
options: The power becomes exactly twice as large
The power stays exactly the same value
The power becomes four times larger
The power becomes half of its old value
mcqs.explain: Doubling V also doubles I in a fixed resistance, so P = V I gives 2 × 2 = 4 times the power.

mcqs.q: The specification states that work is done when charge flows in a circuit. What does this mean?
options: Charge is gradually used up as it goes round the circuit
Energy is transferred as charge is pushed through the components
Work is done only when part of the circuit actually moves
Current is transferred from the battery to the components
mcqs.explain: The supply does work on the charge, and that work is the energy transferred electrically.

mcqs.q: An electric heater has a power of 2000 W and is switched on for 3.0 minutes. How much energy does it transfer?
A current of 0.50 A flows for 600 s through a component with a potential difference of 12 V across it. How much energy is transferred?
Which row gives the correct unit for every quantity in the equation E = Q V?
options: E in joules, Q in amperes, V in volts
E in watts, Q in coulombs, V in volts
E in joules, Q in coulombs, V in volts
E in joules, Q in coulombs, V in ohms
mcqs.explain: These are the units the specification states for energy transferred, charge flow and potential difference.

mcqs.q: A food mixer is plugged into the ac mains and switched on. Which statement best describes the useful energy transfer?
options: Energy is transferred electrically to a chemical energy store
Energy is transferred electrically to a kinetic energy store
Energy is transferred by heating to a kinetic energy store
Energy is transferred from a kinetic store to the mains supply
mcqs.explain: The mains does electrical work on the motor, filling the kinetic store of the rotating blades.

mcqs.q: A cordless drill runs from a rechargeable battery. An identical mains drill runs from the ac mains. Which statement is correct?
options: Only the mains drill transfers energy electrically to a motor
The battery drill uses ac and the mains drill uses dc supply
Only the battery drill can transfer energy to a kinetic store
Both drills transfer energy electrically to a kinetic store
mcqs.explain: Battery and ac mains supplies both do electrical work on the motor, filling its kinetic energy store.

mcqs.q: Appliance A has a power of 1200 W and is used for 5.0 minutes. Appliance B has a power of 400 W and is used for 20 minutes. Which transfers more energy?
options: A, because its power rating is three times that of B
B, because time alone decides the energy transferred
B, because it transfers 480 000 J and A only 360 000 J
Neither, because both are used at the same mains voltage

mcqs.q: A 900 W microwave oven and a 60 W lamp are each switched on for exactly 1.0 minute. Which statement about the energy transferred is correct?
options: The microwave transfers 900 J and the lamp only 60 J
The microwave transfers 54 000 W and the lamp 3600 W
Both transfer the same energy because the times are equal
The microwave transfers 54 000 J and the lamp 3600 J
mcqs.explain: E = P t with t = 60 s gives 900 × 60 = 54 000 J and 60 × 60 = 3600 J.

mcqs.q: What is the National Grid?
options: A system of power stations that generates all of the country's electricity
A system of cables and transformers linking power stations to consumers
A network of cables that stores electricity until consumers need it
A set of step-up transformers that supply homes with electricity
mcqs.explain: This is the definition given in the specification.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly describes where the transformers are used in the National Grid?
options: Step-down transformers near power stations, step-up near homes
Step-up transformers at both ends of the transmission cables
Step-down transformers at both ends of the transmission cables
Step-up transformers near power stations, step-down near consumers
mcqs.explain: Step-up transformers raise the pd onto the transmission cables; step-down transformers lower it for domestic use.

mcqs.q: Why does transferring electrical power at a very high potential difference make the National Grid an efficient way to transfer energy?
options: The current is smaller, so less energy is wasted heating the cables
The current is larger, so more energy reaches the consumers quickly
The resistance of the cables is reduced by the high potential difference
The transformers add extra energy to replace whatever is wasted
mcqs.explain: P = V I means a higher pd needs a smaller current for the same power, and P = I² R then gives a much smaller wasted power.

mcqs.q: A transmission cable has a resistance of 4.0 Ω and carries a current of 100 A. What power is wasted heating the cable?
The same electrical power is transmitted at ten times the potential difference, so the current in the cables falls to one tenth. What happens to the power wasted in the cables?
options: It falls to one tenth
It falls to one hundredth
It falls to a thousandth
It remains unchanged
mcqs.explain: P = I² R and the resistance is unchanged, so scaling the current by 1/10 scales the wasted power by (1/10)² = 1/100.

mcqs.q: A motor connected to a 12 V supply transfers 18 000 J of energy in 60 s. What is the current through the motor?
A charge of 45 C flows through a lamp and 540 J of energy is transferred. What is the potential difference across the lamp?
mcqs.explain: Rearranging E = Q V gives V = E ÷ Q = 540 ÷ 45 = 12 V.

mcqs.q: An electric kettle is connected to the ac mains and boils some water. Which statement describes the main energy transfer?
options: Energy is transferred electrically into the kettle's kinetic store
Energy stored chemically in the mains is transferred to the water
Energy is transferred electrically to the water's thermal store
Energy is transferred by heating from the mains to the element
mcqs.explain: The mains does electrical work on the heating element, which raises the thermal store of the water.

mcqs.q: Which change would exactly double the energy an appliance transfers?
options: Double the power and halve the time it is switched on
Halve the power and keep the time it is on the same
Double the power and double the time it is switched on
Keep the power the same and double the time it is on
mcqs.explain: E = P t, so doubling t with P unchanged doubles the energy transferred.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the National Grid is correct?
options: It transfers electrical power from power stations to consumers
It generates the electrical power that consumers use
It stores electrical power until consumers switch things on
It changes the ac supply from power stations into a dc supply
mcqs.explain: The specification states that electrical power is transferred from power stations to consumers using the National Grid.

mcqs.q: A hairdryer is rated at 1800 W and runs from a 230 V mains supply. What current does it take, and how much energy does it transfer in 2.0 minutes?
options: 7.8 A and 3600 J

mcqs.q: Which quantity is measured in coulombs?
options: The flow of charge past a point
The current in a circuit branch
The energy a device transfers
The potential difference of a cell
mcqs.explain: Charge flow, Q, is measured in coulombs, C.
